queries: Bitcoin whale 2009 wallet sold 1.24 billion BTC February 2026
rounds.what_returned: Round 1 immediately surfaced a debunking article from FX Leaders (Feb 24 2026) titled 'The Truth about Oldest Bitcoin Whale Cashing Out', plus a CCN article asking 'Is It Accurate?'. Results describe the claim as based on a fake/edited screenshot that misrepresented routine Coinbase transactions. The Satoshi Whale 1KFYo wallet did exist and was sending ~40.647 BTC batches to Coinbase, but the narrative framing was misleading.
rounds.lesson: The 'Satoshi Whale' tag and $1.24B figure were real enough to generate significant coverage. The core debunking angle: (1) the screenshot was edited/manipulated, (2) the $1.24B figure conflated network-wide data with a single wallet, (3) the wallet was possibly connected to Coinbase operational infrastructure, and (4) sending to Coinbase does not confirm a sale.

rounds.what_returned: Confirmed multiple independent sources: FX Leaders, CCN/Yahoo Finance, Yellow.com all report the claim was misleading. Key findings: (1) the Arkham screenshot was edited, (2) the wallet may have been a Coinbase hot wallet or exchange-linked address, (3) $1.24B figure was an aggregation of network-wide losses across many wallets, not a single entity. Also found a ZyCrypto article attributing the wallet to 'Owen Gunden' — a named identity claim worth noting.
rounds.lesson: The 'fake screenshot' angle is well-sourced. The wallet did send BTC to Coinbase but: the $1.24B total was fabricated by aggregation; the 'oldest whale' and '2009' provenance is unverified; and the framing 'sold his entire stack' and 'ask yourself why' implies intentional bearish signal-sending which is unsupported.

insights.deepseek_advice: For viral crypto whale claims accompanied by dashboard screenshots, immediately search the specific dollar amount + 'bitcoin whale' + the current year — these sensational claims are almost always debunked within 24-48 hours and the debunking articles rank highly. Identify any visible wallet address labels or platform names in the image description and include them as search terms, as they often serve as unique identifiers linking to fact-check coverage.
